The conjugate of a subgroup G with more than one element is a subgroup where the entire set is a multiplicative subgroup. If the original subgroup is generated by a set S, then its conjugate is generated by S * S⁻¹. This is a result of using the fact that if G is a group, then H.num ∈ G if and only if H.den ∈ G, and hence, H.num and H.den are in the carrier of some element of G.

Defining the direct product of two elements a and b as a * b, it is clear that the direct product of any two elements from the carrier of x is also in the carrier of x, as a = x * h * x⁻¹ and b = x * k * x⁻¹, so a * b = x * (h * k) * x⁻¹. Since h * k is in the carrier of x, this is in the carrier of x.

Finally, to have the entire set as a subgroup, its elements need to be closed under (intersection with S). The conjugate carries this property over because S * S⁻¹ is closed extension.
